Festival

FES-tuh-vuhl · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Festival is a day or period of public celebration.

Our town holds a fall festival with hayrides, games, and caramel apples.

Worked Example

At the spring festival, dancers filled the square while food stands sold dumplings.

Dancers, crowds, and food stands show a big public celebration. A celebration like that is a festival.

How Strong Is It? — Party → Carnival → festival

Party vs. festival

Party vs. festival: A party is smaller: a birthday party fits in one backyard.

Carnival vs. festival

Carnival vs. festival: A carnival is even bigger and louder, with rides and games that can take over a whole fairground.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — festiv

root — festiv: feast, holiday (Latin (festum))

suffix — al

suffix — al: the act or result of (builds a noun here) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Festiv- means feast or holiday, and here -al builds a noun: a festival is a holiday-style celebration.

Use the root in a new word: feast

Use the root in a new word: feast: For the harvest feast, the whole family cooked all day.

Root Check

Word Choice

Here -al helps build a noun - a festival is a thing (a celebration), not a describing word. Use festival for big public celebrations, not small private parties.
